Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
1237 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Updated Aviation section

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Residual coastal flooding possible for south shore locations
with minor coastal flooding likely for Western Sound locations
as high tide approaches. Beach flooding and dune erosion 
may continue through early this afternoon.

2) Rainfall anticipated today and Sunday night into early Monday 
morning. No adverse impacts anticipated.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Coastal Flood Advisories remains effect, but high tide has 
largely passed for south shore locations. Residual minor
flooding remains possible as water levels recede here. 
Approaching high tide for Western Sound will bring another round
of minor coastal flooding. 

Beach flooding and dune erosion will continue through early this
afternoon with the swell direction becoming briefly 
perpendicular to the coast. Breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet 
gradually diminish through the day with ocean seas diminishing 
and the direction becoming more SW.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
500mb low and attendant surface low pass to our NW through northern 
NY today. Embedded shortwaves aloft and upward forcing with the 
proximity of the surface low combined with residual moisture will 
bring light rainfall and showers to the area today with the highest 
overall chances NW of the city. SW winds gust 20-30 mph today.

Rain is then expected Sunday night into early Monday with low 
pressure tracking NW form the eastern Great Lakes to Northern New 
England. Some models also depict a secondary low or triple point 
potentially moving through the forecast area during this period. 
Expecting rainfall, with the highest probability of occurrence 
during the late night hours of Sunday night. Probably looking at 
about a half inch of rainfall, so no hydrologic impacts anticipated. 
A low level jet associated with the secondary low/triple point may 
help contribute to gusty winds as well as a slight chance of thunder 
with some elevated instability noted in some guidance. Right now any 
wind impacts would appear to be minimal.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
The terminals will remain between departing low pressure and 
high pressure to the south through Saturday.

Flight categories will fluctuate between VFR and MVFR through
the TAF period. The best chance for VFR is this evening through
overnight, especially for NYC terminals. During periods of 
MVFR, ceilings may range from 025-030 with some outlying 
terminals briefly falling to around 020. There is also a chance 
for a few showers this afternoon/early evening. Brief MVFR vsby 
is possible in these showers. 

SSW winds 15-20 kt with gusts around 25 kt this afternoon and
early evening. Peak gusts could reach 30 kt at times, especially
at NYC and coastal terminals. Winds veer to the SW-W tonight
with winds weakening a bit, but gusts around 20 kt still
possible at NYC terminals. Gusts at outlying terminals may drop
off late tonight/early Saturday. W winds around 15 kt with gusts
20-25 kt expected after 13z.  

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 
Fluctuations between VFR and MVFR possible this afternoon/early
evening. Brief period of MVFR possible overnight. 

Confidence in MVFR prevailing Saturday is low and there is a
chance VFR prevails more of the day than currently indicated. 

Wind gusts could briefly drop off at JFK, LGA, and EWR 06z-13z.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Saturday through Wednesday... 

Saturday Afternoon: MVFR ceilings possible. W winds G20-25kt, 
diminishing in the evening and at night.

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night-Monday: Rain likely with MVFR or lower conditions 
after midnight through early Monday morning. Rain could persist
east of NYC terminals after sunrise, but improving conditions
likely through the day. S winds G20-30 kt late Sunday night,
then W G 25-35 kt on Monday. Winds diminish Monday Night.

Tuesday-Wednesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Gale Warnings in effect through tonight on the ocean waters with SCA 
on the non ocean waters for the same time period. SCA conds likely 
follow on the ocean for Saturday, and possibly for the non ocean 
waters as well. While the forecast on the non ocean waters 
advertises gusts to 25kt during Saturday, have decided to wait on 
extending the SCA here into Saturday as it's in the 3rd period and 
it's also possible that pressure gradient over the area trends 
weaker. Ocean seas today remain quite elevated due to residual 
swell, which should impact the entrances of LI Sound and NY Harbor 
for much of the day. Outside of residual swell on the ocean during 
the morning, sub-advisory conditions are expected on all waters for 
Sunday. Winds and seas then ramp up Sunday night into Monday with 
the approach and passage of a low pressure system. Gales on the 
ocean waters are anticipated, and possibly some non-ocean zones 
could see a few gale force gusts. Will include mention of this for 
the ocean waters in the HWO for the time being.
